Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: I take from Operating posture - Ergonomics Design Considerations (E55, Operating posture - Ergonomics Design Considerations) that hand used, grip posture and duration change grip coordination, and I take from Review of Hand/Wrist/Arm Ergonomics Analysis Methods: Part 1 (E56, Review of Hand/Wrist/Arm Ergonomics Analysis Methods: Part 1) that continuous handgrip above 10 percent of Maximum Voluntary Contraction (MVC, meaning maximum voluntary contraction) and intermittent grip above 17 percent MVC were unacceptable.
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: The numbers that decide it are total slope load 401 N from the slope load from total weight times sine theta (E97) needing total lock torque 74.2 N m from the total lock torque slope times cluster radius (E98), which needs 1.55 kN clamp from the clamp for corrected total torque (E100) superseding 1.40 kN in the locked cluster holding torque and disc clamp on steep stair (E51) because that used the lighter mass, giving 57.4 N finger force from the corrected hand release force (E101) with caliper ratio 8, lever ratio 4.5 and cable efficiency 0.75 including friction loss, against the maximum manual lever force of 29 lb or 129 N I take from Force Guidelines (E78), with factor 2.25, but above the 9 lb pinch limit so it needs a power grip at 3.8 to 6.4 centimetre (cm) span with wrist extension 25 degrees or less and neutral posture I take from Review of Hand/Wrist/Arm Ergonomics Analysis Methods (E56), and parked shear demand ratio 0.498 from the park pin shear with dynamic allowance (E102) for factor about 2.0 with impact allowance on the steepest slope, where Maximum Voluntary Contraction (MVC) fatigue rules say continuous grip above 10 percent (%) MVC is unacceptable from the same review, which is why hands-off auto-lock with no grip effort matters.
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: The numbers that decide it are total slope load 401 N from the slope load from total weight times sine theta (E97) needing total lock torque 74.2 N m from the total lock torque slope times cluster radius (E98), which needs 1.55 kN clamp from the clamp for corrected total torque (E100) because braking torque is pad force times friction times rotor radius I take from The Bicycle Physics of the Hydraulic Brake (E111), giving 57.4 N finger force from the corrected hand release force (E101) with caliper ratio 8, lever ratio 4.5 and cable efficiency 0.75 including friction loss, against maximum manual lever force 29 pounds (lb) I take from Force Guidelines (E78) with factor 2.25 but above maximum pinch force 9 lb, so it needs power grip at 3.8 to 6.4 centimetre span with wrist extension 25 degrees or less I take from Review of Hand/Wrist/Arm Ergonomics Analysis Methods: Part 1 (E56) where continuous grip above 10 percent of MVC is unacceptable, like lifting a 5.85 kg bag with two fingers, and parked shear demand ratio 0.498 from the park pin shear with dynamic allowance (E102) for factor about 2.0 with impact on the steepest slope.
